text:
sara: Heads up — after landing the RoPE scale adjustment (PR #4527) we're seeing a noticeable tail-latency bump on mistral-8x7b with our sliding-window config. Traces point to frequent kernel-selector flips and KV cache churn.

matt: Oof. Where did you see it (hosted/dedicated), and what numbers are we talking about?

sara: Dedicated cluster (pinned GPUs). p50 unchanged, but p95 for generation at seq=2048 went from ~120ms -> ~150ms on the canary fleet. Heap of small traces show repeated kernel selection calls for attention with 1-token seq_len deltas.

devon: That smells like seq-boundary flips. If sliding-window shifts the attention window across tile boundaries, the kernel chooser can bounce between different tiled kernels (e.g. 64 vs 32 tiles). These flips also cause different KV tiling/layouts so the cache fingerprint changes and we lose locality. Seen something similar during Mixtral tuning.

lia: Also note the RoPE scaling change adjusts rotary multipliers around mid layers — subtle FP differences can push codepaths (quant-friendly vs fallback) and lead to different kernel choices. Not common but possible.

ops-bot: perf-deploy: deploy/rope-scale-adjust merged by devon at 2026-03-18T09:12Z (canary: 12 nodes).

matt: Short-term mitigation ideas: add hysteresis to kernel_selector thresholds, or prefer stable kernels for sliding_window workloads. Can we add a per-request knob to pin kernel selection?

sara: Quick experiments: increasing kernel hysteresis from 8 -> 64 tokens reduced flip-rate, p95 improved from 150ms -> ~135ms. Biggest improvement came from enabling prefix/KV fingerprinting so reused KV shards survive sliding boundaries. Config snippet I tested: 

```
runtime:
  kv_cache:
    enable_prefix_fingerprint: true
  kernel_selector:
    hysteresis_tokens: 64
```

After those tweaks p95 is ~125ms on same traffic.

devon: Good. Long-term we should: 1) add unit/regression tests that simulate sliding-window token shifts, 2) emit telemetry for kernel_switch_count and kv_cache_miss_by_prefix, 3) consider a kernel preference policy that trades a small p50 cost for stability (less thrash).

lia: I'll open a follow-up issue with test vectors + config flags and assign to @devon and @sara. Also propose a canary that pins the old RoPE scale so we can A/B.

sara: Will add telemetry: kernel_switch_count per request + kv_prefix_fingerprint_hit boolean. That will tell us if the cache is the main culprit.

matt: If customers are impacted we should consider reverting the RoPE change until we have canary telemetry, otherwise continue monitoring.

sara: Not urgent for support yet, but on watch. Will post updates here and in #eng-runtime when telemetry shows clear correlation. :thumbsup:
